add.text: Page has 150 methods in one bag

add.title: The problem
add.text: Page 97, Item 30, Events 5. About 50 of Page's only pass a call on to a helper. Voice sees 9 (the help hides the rest); anyone reading the code sees all 150.

add.title: On /live/, tabs and columns don't draw
add.text: LivePage draws its own screen and skips the frame that draws tabs, columns and nav. A widget that draws itself would work on any page.
Idea 1: UI lives in modules, imported on need

add.title: What changes
add.text: Sidebar, header, nav, tabs, columns and previews each become one file. A page imports only the ones it uses. Page itself keeps data, url and children.

add.title: In code
add.text: `import "/framework/core/Page/ui/Tabs.js";` in the page's class file. Nothing loads that no page asked for.

add.title: Good / cost
add.text: Smallest Page. But code still needs a way to reach the widget, and where its state is saved is left open.
Idea 2: one door, page.ui

add.title: What changes
add.text: `page.ui.tabs` is made the first time it is touched, already wired to the page. Page gains one name instead of fifty.

add.title: From voice
add.text: `{"ui": {"tabs": {"selected": "Idea 2"}}}`. That line is saved in the page's log, so a reload shows the same tab.

add.title: Good / cost
add.text: State is saved for free, and the help shows `ui` once. Alone, though, every widget would be loaded on every page.
Recommended: both together

add.title: How they fit
add.text: Modules are where the code lives (idea 1). `page.ui` is how a page reaches them and saves their state (idea 2). A widget loads when the page's class imports it; `page.ui` only offers what loaded.

add.title: Try it
add.text: The tab bar above is the prototype: `page.ui.tabs`. Say "switch to Idea 1" and voice sends one line; reload and it stays.

add.title: If yes, next
add.text: Move tabs, columns and previews off Page into `core/Page/ui/`, one widget at a time, old names kept as shortcuts. About $15–25.

add.title: Overview has no heading; Alpha does
add.text: Overview is `tabs()`'s `home` tab — it renders the PARENT page's own content directly (Frame.js:19 `this.tabs({ home: () => this.box() })`), no page wrapper, no h1. Alpha/Beta are separate full `Page` objects (own `page.jsonl`, own `title`), rendered via `child.render()` inside the panel (Frame.js region()) — `Page.class.js:564` `if (this.title) h1.c("page-title", this.title)` fires for them, not for the home tab's bare content box.

add.title: The explorer widget only draws for a REAL page.jsonl page
add.text: `Jsonl.js load()`: `if (!page.has_content()) page.content.fallback(page.log_view)` — only pages literally loaded from a `page.jsonl` file (Overview/the parent, Alpha, Beta) get this fallback, which draws `draw_folder()` (the tree+data split, `ext/files/files.js`). Gamma was created purely by a `{"tab":{"name":"gamma",...}}` line (`Jsonl.js tab()` → `page.add(name,data)`, Page.class.js:326) — a plain in-memory `Page`, never run through `Jsonl.load`, so it never gets `content.fallback` and the explorer never draws.

add.title: "Files · N" and /files/ are generic, on every titled page
add.text: `Page.class.js:590` adds the chip (`PageFilesTab.chip`) to EVERY page with a `title`+`url` and no `no_files` — that includes Gamma, which is why it still shows "Files · 2" with no inline explorer. The `/files/` route itself comes from `Page.class.js:398`, inside `child()`: any page's `files/` child auto-resolves to `PageFilesTab.route(this)` (`FilesTab.js:43`) unless a real `files/` folder exists.

add.title: Alpha can't scroll to the bottom — found the rule
add.text: `public/styles.css:299-300`: `.pages:not(:has(> .page.active-page)):not(:has(> .default)) { overflow-y: hidden; }`. It assumes the active leaf is always a DIRECT child of the scrolling `.pages` region. A tabs page keeps every tab's content inside the SAME `.page`/`.pages` region (no extra region opens — `ext/tabs` just swaps a panel) — so the leaf is marked `.active-ancestor` several levels down, never a direct `.active-page` child, and this rule hides the one region that should scroll. Measured in a headless worktree check: `.pages` scrollHeight 909 vs clientHeight 649, computed `overflow-y: hidden`. Out of my fence (public/styles.css) — the Phase B fix scrolls the PAGE itself instead, inside core/Page/Page.css.

add.title: Voice and tab content — what decides it today
add.text: Today: a `{"tab":{"name","title",...}}` line with no own folder makes a bare `Page` (title only, no content, no explorer) — that's Gamma..Eta. A tab with a REAL `name/page.jsonl` child (Alpha, Beta) gets a full page: its own title, explorer, files. Recommended smallest delta: let a `tab` line carry `"content"` as a short markdown/text string (`Jsonl.js tab()` already extracts `content` from the object at line 106, it's just unused when there's no existing child Page to apply it to — only the "already a Page" branch at line 117-121 uses it). Wire the FIRST branch (line 126, fresh `page.add`) to pass `content` through too, so `{"tab":{"name":"gamma","content":"some words"}}` shows text in the tab with no folder needed. Alternative (not recommended): make voice create a real `gamma/page.jsonl` child file — gives the full explorer for free but is heavier for a one-line tab and not what voice usually wants.

add.title: Indexes: what's missing
add.text:
- No per-page index.jsonl: files.jsonl still lists files, not titles or descriptions.
- No reader loads children's previews one level deep; each page is loaded whole.
- The session preview index (one line per session, indexing-2026-10-08 section 2) is proposed, not built.

add.title: What a parent loads today
add.text:
Every direct child, recursively, 2 levels deep by default — the WHOLE file, every line, replayed (`Page.class.js:681` `depth = 2`, `:685-696` `load_all_children()`; `Jsonl.js:28-52` fetches; `Store.js:208-212` plain `fetch()`, no range, `parse()` every line). Measured against this worktree's server:
```
url                                          jsonl  KB     last-req
/live/                                       2      3.7    ~0.9s
/live/design/                                2      3.7    ~0.3s
/framework/core/Page/                        168    119    ~1.2s
/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/           118    1847   ~1.0s
```
Every number here is from a live headless run against the worktree, not estimated.

add.title: 1000 files: what happens
add.text:
Synthetic tree (4 levels, 5 children/level, 156 pages, 20 lines each; built and measured in this worktree, deleted after): default `depth=2` fetched 31 distinct `page.jsonl` (root + its 5 children + their 25 children), 31 KB, last request at ~1.2s. The 125 leaves at level 4 were never fetched — depth=2 bounds the cost of a NESTED tree no matter how big it gets below that.
```
shape                real risk
nested (deep)         bounded: only 2 levels load, ever
flat (1 level, N=1000) NOT bounded: all N direct children load on first open
```
A flat folder of 1000 cards (no sub-folders) is the dangerous case: `load_all_children()` walks EVERY name in `this.children` at once, no pagination. Extrapolating from the real `/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/` measurement (118 files → 1.85 MB, last request 968ms): 1000 flat children → roughly 16 MB and, because Chromium caps at ~6 connections per host, a last-request time in the TENS OF SECONDS, not ~1s — the wait scales with file COUNT more than bytes.

add.title: What makes a folder today
add.text:
```
path                                    what it does                                   file:line
create_page / pages.add                 mkdir + writes <name>/page.jsonl line 1        Servex/agents/Subpages.js:46-58
Item.move_to({url, path})               leaves a {moved_to} forward on the item         core/Item/Item.js:513-523
move_item() (the node-side handoff)     carries the item's lines to the new file        Servex/agents/page_tools.js:771
an agent writing files by hand          /live/design/ itself was made this way          (no tool, no link line)
NOT a folder path: LivePage.save()      keeps a screen embedded in /live/page.jsonl      public/live/LivePage.js:84-92
```
The brief guessed LivePage.save() makes a folder — it doesn't; corrected in the doc.

add.title: Proposed: when a card becomes a folder
add.text:
No auto-upgrade exists today — every folder above is deliberate. Size and "gaining sub-items" alone don't force one: nested Items (`{"k2":{"answers":{"add":…}}}`) already live inside one `page.jsonl`.

**Recommended trigger: promote the instant a card needs a sidecar it can't hold embedded** — a file attached to it, or `pages.add` aimed at one of ITS OWN embedded children (a grandchild needing its own folder has nowhere to live inside one file — `CHILD` regex, `Listing.js:6`, only names a real `page.jsonl`).

**Alternative, named not recommended: size** (a KB/line threshold, periodic sweep) — fires on a schedule instead of the cause, so it's early or late, never exact.

**Who moves it:** `Item.move_to({url:"/live/foo/"})` (`Item.js:513`) → `move_item()` (`page_tools.js:771`) — the same function already named for "break a card out".
**Left behind:** a `Ref` (`core/Item/Ref.js`) at the old embedded slot.
**Naming:** slug = folder name = path segment (the card's existing id); title stays separate; a link always shows the title, never the slug.
